20A.9 Ministers are to teach the people all the laws and statutes of God.

precepts.text: Go ye therefore, and teach all nations: teach the Israelites scattered in all nations. That is the prophecy, and that is why IUIC travels to all these countries and just carried out one of the biggest worldwide blitzes: to bring back our people to who they are.
precepts.point: And I will bring you again into the place whence I caused you to be carried away captive: that is Jerusalem. That is our land. Everything you see here is temporary. You already know the end of the movie; you win. So why are you bugging out? Last week the Bishop was teaching how some of us turn to liquor to deal with the hatred and the trauma. You have to expect the hatred; the problem is you are dying to be loved by people who will never love you.

note.label: Why They Hated US: Walking in the Footsteps of the Persecuted

precepts.why:
“And I will be found of you, saith the Lord: and I will turn away your captivity, and I will gather you from all the nations”. Why does it say from all nations? This is for the Israelite who says there is no Israelite in Africa. No matter where you go on the planet, you are going to find some Israelite; that is why he says all nations, “and from all the places whither I have driven you”.

That is why Christ said, “Go ye therefore, and teach all nations”. Teach the Israelites, because we were scattered in all nations. That is the prophecy. And no matter where we are, we are going to be hated.

That is why IUIC travels to all these countries: to bring our people back to who they are and tell them they are the Israelites. That is why we just had one of the biggest worldwide blitzes, because we understand the scripture and we follow it. As John saw, Christ redeemed us to God by his blood out of every kindred, tongue, people and nation, and the Lord will bring us again into the place whence he caused us to be carried away captive.

precepts.text: Go ye therefore, and teach all nations: because we were scattered into all nations, we have to be taught in all nations. That's why you see the bishop giving the order: look historically where our people were slaves, and train them how to behave for God, to establish the kingdom, because they've been trained after the ways of their colonizers.
precepts.point: A land which the Lord thy God careth for: the eyes of the Lord thy God are always upon it.

note.label: Are You A Strong Independent Woman?

precepts.why:
Amos 9:9 says, “I will sift the house of Israel among all nations”. Christians read Matthew 28:19 and think it means make everyone disciples: “Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost”.

This is what it means: because we were scattered into all nations, we have to be taught in all nations. It is the same sifting Amos speaks of. Christ himself, when he started his ministry, told the twelve, “Go not into the way of the Gentiles”, but “go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.” Teaching all nations is going into all the nations where the lost sheep were scattered.

That is why the bishop gives the order: look historically at where our people were slaves, and go there and train them how to behave for God, to establish the kingdom. They have been trained after the ways of their colonizers, so we must train them in the word of God. The brothers who travel find the hardest thing is telling oppressed people that Jesus Christ is not a white man, because that white Jesus, made up in the Renaissance, is how the colonizers modified their behavior. But the charge stands: tell our people, you are not black, not Hispanic, not West Indian, not African; you are the lost sheep of the house of Israel.

precepts.text: Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you. Christ said all nations because we are scattered in all of them, and the pastors further the scattering.
precepts.point: I have seen in the prophets of Jerusalem an horrible thing: they commit adultery, walk in lies, and strengthen the hands of evildoers, that none doth return from his wickedness. When Jamal Bryant was checked over his wife's dress he doubled down, so when we tell his congregants on the street to repent, they double down too. They are all to God as Sodom, and he will feed them wormwood and gall.

note.label: There Is No Hate Like Christian Love

precepts.why:
“Woe be unto the pastors that destroy and scatter the sheep of my pasture! saith the Lord.” “Ye have scattered my flock, and driven them away, and have not visited them”. The pastors keep the confusion and the sin in the black community going. They keep Ephraim separated from Judah; our bands are cast asunder, and they are not bringing it back. They are furthering the scattering of the children of Israel, not bringing us together.

So look what Christ had to come and say: “Go ye therefore, and teach all nations”. Why all nations? Because we are scattered in all nations, and the pastors are furthering the scattering. Christ sends his disciples out to the scattered sheep in every country, “Teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you”: the very commandments the pastors say are done away with.

That is the other half of Jeremiah 23: “I will gather the remnant of my flock out of all countries whither I have driven them, and will bring them again to their folds”, “And I will set up shepherds over them which shall feed them”. Where the pastors scatter and teach that the law is gone, the Lord sends shepherds to go into all nations and teach his people to observe everything he commanded.

precepts.text: The angel of the Lord descended, rolled back the stone, and sat upon it; his countenance was like lightning and his raiment white as snow, and for fear of him the keepers did shake and became as dead men.
precepts.point: She repeated the message: the child shall be a Nazarite to God from the womb to the day of his death, and she was to drink no wine nor strong drink nor eat any unclean thing.

note.label: Judges 13: A Nazarite from the Womb

precepts.why:
The woman said the man’s “countenance was like the countenance of an angel of God, very terrible”. Verse 3 says it was the angel of the Lord, but he did not tell her, so she was not sure; she only knew his face was terrible like an angel’s. See what an angel’s countenance is: “the angel of the Lord descended from heaven, and came and rolled back the stone from the door, and sat upon it. His countenance was like lightning, and his raiment white as snow: And for fear of him the keepers did shake, and became as dead men.”

The popular pictures of angels as cute babies with smooth cheeks and little white wings do not match the biblical descriptions at all. Grown men, the keepers at the sepulchre, shook and became as dead men. To see an angel of the Most High was a terrifying sight, not something to jump for joy about, and that is just how Manoah’s wife described the one that came to her.
